page: Microsoft Azure M32-16ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-bound enterprise systems. Powered by Intel Xeon 8280M processors with x86_64 architecture operating at a base clock of 2.7 GHz, the instance allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 38 MB L3 cache. Memory density is exceptionally high, supplying 875.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 54.69 GB per vCPU. Hardware virtualization is mediated via Microsoft Hyper-V, and the server comes equipped with a bundled 1100 GB local SSD volume, with no hardware GPUs attached.

Benchmark measurements indicate distinct execution characteristics between single-threaded and parallel tasks. Single-threaded metrics, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core, register in the lower 25 percent of tested systems, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 10 percent. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks show average throughput, matching expectations for an 8-core, 16-thread Intel platform. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 74.4 GB/sec for 256 MB block reads and 37.98 GB/sec for writes, placing memory throughput in the middle 50 percent range. In-memory application tests demonstrate reliable throughput, highlighted by Redis SET execution exceeding 10.43 million operations per second.

The qualitative efficiency profile reflects a specialized architecture prioritized for extreme memory footprints rather than high-frequency raw computation. Running a high RAM-to-CPU ratio allows organizations to consolidate large datasets without paying for surplus compute cores that would otherwise remain idle. Consequently, the M32-16ms is ideally suited for in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise relational database management systems, and large analytics processing requiring substantial data residency in memory.

Featuring a vast memory allocation of 875.0 GB, the instance yields an extreme ratio of 54.69 GB of RAM per vCPU, supported by an integrated 1100 GB local SSD for transient storage. Synthetic benchmarks establish that while single-core processing and compression rates fall within lower percentiles, multi-threaded tasks and uncached memory bandwidth maintain solid mid-tier output. Synthetic database metrics demonstrate balanced operation, highlighted by Redis throughput reaching 10.43 million SET operations per second. Lacking dedicated accelerators, this configuration optimizes operational spending by focusing capacity on memory density rather than excess compute. It is well-fitted for large-scale in-memory databases, extensive caching layers, SAP workloads, and data-heavy enterprise applications requiring immediate in-memory state retention.
